evidence: app/app/routes.ts:11 — abilities route is a single removable line; no nav link exists (root.tsx:22)
app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:264 — Abilities section + loader mapping at :160 are the only in-page references
app/app/lib/types.ts:9 — `hidden?: boolean` on Card exists only for the ability page
app/app/lib/api.server.ts:139 — `extra` callback parameter used only by ability.tsx:27
app/app/components/PokemonCards.tsx:23 — 'Hidden ability' note + app.css:219 .card__note become dead code
removability.rationale: Dropping abilities is nearly delete-file-plus-one-line, but the hidden-ability feature leaks shared type fields, a generic parameter and CSS in four other files that would go dead.

evidence: app/app/lib/api.server.ts:39 — spriteUrl is the single sprite source; all card lists build through speciesCard (:119) and pokemonCards (:136)
app/app/lib/api.server.ts:148 — card sort covers move/ability/type lists, but home.tsx:66-69 orders via index.species, so a sort change touches two places
app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:43 vs app/app/routes/move.tsx:8 — `type Move` declared twice with divergent fields; API shape changes must be made in both
app/app/routes/home.tsx:65-92 — filter logic via DOM refs, a debounce timer and two hydration-fix effects; a search bug fix requires reasoning about stale closures and uncontrolled inputs
changeability.rationale: Data bugs mostly land in one obvious helper, but home's ref-driven filter code is the hardest-to-modify part of the app, and the duplicated Move type means some API changes are made twice.

evidence: app/app/lib/api.server.ts:1 — server access isolated in a .server.ts module, imported only by route loaders (grep: 6 route files, no components)
app/app/lib/types.ts:1-11 — Card/TypeInfo are narrow serializable seams between loader shaping and client rendering
app/app/components/MoveTable.tsx:16-31 — MoveRow + Column interfaces keep the table independent of API details
app/app/routes/not-found.tsx:3-9 — 404 stub route renders null and throws; the real UI lives in root.tsx:60, an indirection a maintainer must discover
app/app/components/Section.tsx:8 — hardcodes the 'panel' class, coupling a generic component to global CSS naming
coupling.rationale: Server/client separation is exemplary for this size and components depend on narrow data types; a few small tangles (404 UI living in root, CSS class baked into Section) keep it from 5.

evidence: app/app/lib/api.server.ts:77-118 — getIndex is a genuine abstraction (species, types, generations, cross-referenced slots) reused by five routes
app/app/lib/api.server.ts:136-148 — pokemonCards(index, refs, extra?) absorbs the real variation across type/move/ability lists including hidden-ability without flag creep
app/app/components/MoveTable.tsx:38-52 — declarative COLUMNS + sort state; showLevel is the only boolean flag and it maps to real spec variation
app/app/routes/move.tsx:48-77 — detail-page skeleton (facts dl + Effect + count + cards) duplicated with ability.tsx:37-51 rather than extracted
app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:81 — versionGroupOrders() is a route-local API helper; a similar page (items) would copy it
abstraction_design.rationale: The data and table abstractions are designed around the app's real variation and stretch well, but page-level structure is copy-paste between move/ability (and would be for items), and API record types are inlined per route instead of shared.

findings.issue: Filter state is managed through DOM refs, a manual debounce timer and two effects that patch pre-hydration input and back/forward sync; this is the fragile, non-idiomatic corner of the app (framework guidance favors `<Form method="get">` or controlled state for URL-backed filters).
findings.suggestion: Use controlled inputs driven by loaderData, or a `<Form method="get">` with fetcher/useSubmit for the debounce, letting React Router own URL/state sync; the hydration-fix effects then disappear.

findings.issue: `type Move` is declared inline here and again at move.tsx:8 with different fields, so API shape changes require editing two route files.
findings.suggestion: Move API record types (Move, VersionGroup, TypeRecord is already shared) into lib/types.ts and import them where needed.

findings.issue: versionGroupOrders() plus the game-selection, move fan-out and per-method grouping (~90 lines) all live inside the pokemon route module; any similar list+detail page would copy this pattern.
findings.suggestion: Extract move/version-group data assembly into lib/moves.server.ts alongside api.server.ts so the route module is loader glue plus rendering.

findings.issue: The hidden-ability flow is the only consumer of Card.hidden (lib/types.ts:9), the PokemonCards note (components/PokemonCards.tsx:23) and the `extra` parameter of pokemonCards (lib/api.server.ts:139); removing abilities strands dead code in four shared files.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable now, but if abilities ever go, remember to prune the shared plumbing, not just the route.

findings.issue: The not-found route's component renders null and its loader throws 404; the actual 404 markup is exported as NotFound from root.tsx:60 — the 'page' a maintainer looks for is a stub.
findings.suggestion: Move the NotFound UI into routes/not-found.tsx (root ErrorBoundary can still catch data-404s and render it via a shared component or re-export).

findings.issue: Page titles are rendered as JSX `<title>` elements instead of the framework's `meta` export, in every route; it works via React 19 hoisting and is consistent, but deviates from the documented convention and leaves `<Meta />` (root.tsx:13) permanently empty.
findings.suggestion: Either adopt `meta` exports (typed via Route.MetaArgs) for one conventional mechanism, or document the choice in a comment; no functional change needed.

findings.issue: Section hardcodes the `panel` class into every section, coupling a generic layout component to one global CSS style.
findings.suggestion: Let callers pass the class (or default `panel` but allow override without string-concatenation of two sources).

summary: This is a cleanly factored app for its size: all API access, caching and card construction live in one server module, and shared components take narrow serializable props, so most fixes and data-source changes land in one obvious place. The weaknesses are concentrated: home's ref-driven filter code is fragile, the pokemon route module is a monolith with route-local API helpers, and detail-page skeletons plus inline API types would get copied for an Items section. I'd merge it with comments asking for the Move type to be deduplicated and the moves data assembly extracted.
